title: year 5 · the ranges
hook: the Gita's last instruction isn't an order: reflect, then choose
tomorrow: five years walked. what will you carry down the mountain?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a teaching role in the house: a father who said I don't know, and went out to learn. Today, the last day of year five, and the top of the ranges.
screen: `I DON'T KNOW EITHER.` · `TODAY: THE TOP OF THE RANGES.`

segments.voice: The night before someone leaves home, the advice comes in a flood: call, eat real food, don't trust that one friend. Near the end of the Gita's last chapter, Krishna has said everything he came to say. Arjuna is still standing in the chariot, the armies still waiting. And the teacher's last instruction, in this verse, isn't another rule. It's a handoff.
screen: `THE NIGHT BEFORE LEAVING.` → `THE LAST CHAPTER.` → `NOT A RULE. A HANDOFF.`

segments.voice: Krishna says: I have told you wisdom more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully. Then do as you choose. A few verses later Arjuna answers: my confusion is gone. By your grace my memory has come back. I stand firm. Memory, smriti, regained: not something new arriving, but something he had, returning. A neighbor tradition ends its long teaching in a similar place. Near the end of Deuteronomy, Moses speaks to the people before they cross the river: "I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live." Shared: after all the teaching, the choice is put in the listener's hands, and the teacher trusts them with it. And an honest difference. Moses speaks to a whole people, and names his hope in the same breath: choose life. Krishna's verse speaks to one friend and leaves it open; only afterward does he urge Arjuna to take refuge in him. Five years on this path ran a little like that. First words, the stories, the Upanishads and the Yoga Sutras, the epics and the saints, the goddess and the schools, and this year the sources. None of it came as a verdict to sign. It ends, as the Gita's verse does, with: reflect fully, then choose.
screen: `REFLECT FULLY, THEN CHOOSE.` · `SMRITI: MEMORY, REGAINED.` · `MOSES: CHOOSE LIFE.` · `FIVE YEARS, YOURS TO WEIGH.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write one line you're carrying down from this path: a word, a story, a sentence someone said. Read it once, slowly. If you pray, you can offer it back with thanks; if not, let it rest on the page, the way Arjuna's memory came back.
Year 5: the year of reading the sources, ending at the top of the ranges with a handoff: reflect fully, then choose.
Your line: year 5 · the ranges. The choice is in your hands now. Five years, walked.

screen: `DAY 1791 COUNTS.` → `YEAR 5 · THE RANGES, WALKED.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT WILL YOU CARRY DOWN THE MOUNTAIN?`

Wisdom shape, unity thread: shared with Judaism and Christianity, in their own words and source (Deuteronomy 30:19, KJV): at the end of a long teaching, the choice is put in the listener's hands. Honest difference: Moses speaks to a whole people and names his hope ('choose life'); Krishna's verse speaks to one friend and leaves it open, and only afterward urges refuge in him (18.65–66). Never 'the same'; neither ranked; the myth's 'exactly the same thing' is the skimmer's pick. KJV 30:19 opens 'I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that'; the quotation starts at 'I have set'. 'Before they cross the river' is the setting of Deuteronomy generally (the Jordan); confirm the phrasing.
